newsitem.title: USA: GTE Q3 domestic access lines grew 7.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: GTE Q3 domestic access lines grew 7.4 pct.

text.p: GTE Corp on Wednesday said its third quarter domestic access lines rose 7.4 percent from a year earlier, with over half the growth from additional lines to the home.

Domestic cellular subscribers rose 20.4 percent from a year ago to 3.39 million, while overseas users rose 36 percent to 631,000. Domestic cellular revenues rose to $607 million from $530 million a year ago.
The quarterly earnings per share of $0.78 was exactly in line with First Call's analyst consensus, and compared with $0.71, before a one cent gain, a year ago.
Access lines per employee, a productivity measure, grew by 17 percent from a year earlier.
GTE said its domestic cellular marketing strategy to acquire and retain its best customers produced good results.
"Since late last year, our churn has been reduced by over 18 percent and our revenue per subscriber per month has been stable," said GTE chief executive Charles Lee.

"In long distance we've more than doubled the customer base we had just three months ago to over 500,000 customers," Lee said. Unlike regional Bells, GTE is already able to offer long distance and local services in the same regions.
GTE said revenues from advanced services like Caller ID, voice messaging and data services, together with long distance and internet access, were up 40 percent over a year ago.

Lee said GTE was pleased by the operational improvements of its Venezuelan venture CANTV, and this coupled with rate increase and a stablizing economy in that country had a positive impact on GTE's own results. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
